interactions.summary: After a student limits Dante's entry to influence through the work, Jiang generalizes the experience into a theory of great art as universal consciousness that can gradually possess readers and reveal unimaginable things.

Prompted by a student, Jiang inventories his own transformations from years with the Divine Comedy: bodily lightness, release from urban rage, imaginative teaching visions, a sense of mission, and a transcendence akin to flight.

claims.claim: Jiang defines great art as something that enters universal consciousness and can, through long practice, take possession of readers in a way comparable to religion or psychedelics.
Jiang says sustained immersion in the Divine Comedy makes him feel physically lighter and dissolves the anger, claustrophobia, and resentment produced by daily life in Beijing.
Jiang claims long practice with Dante produces controllable visions that feed his teaching, so that imaginative scenes and interpretive ideas arrive on demand when he needs to teach a canto.
Jiang says deep reading of Dante yields a mission to spread Dante's vision of love and to change the world for the better, accompanied by gratitude and responsibility.
Jiang predicts that readers who stay with the Divine Comedy over time will begin to feel a similar ascent, as though lifting themselves toward heaven and participating in transcendence.

signature_moments.moment: The poem is said to make everyday anger and memory float away until the reader feels himself rising toward heaven.
signature_moments.source_phrase: those memories, for whatever reason, they just float away, and then I feel I'm floating upwards
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the strongest bodily image in Jiang's self-testimony about Dante's effects.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang says Dante and the universe feed him visions, and that with enough practice he can summon the right one for a canto almost on command.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It crystallizes the packet's most consequential claim about literary practice becoming an inspired method of teaching.

signature_moments.moment: Dante is imagined smiling from heaven while charging Jiang with a mission to spread the poem's message of love.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Dante is smiling at me from the heavens
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the packet's fusion of vocation, gratitude, and supernatural sanction.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's term for the transpersonal field that great art enters and then mediates to readers over long practice.
Jiang's summary word for the upward, light, almost flying sensation produced by reading Dante well.

chronology_notes.note: This is the lecture's fullest first-person testimony about what multi-year Dante practice has done to Jiang, moving from speculative possession language into explicit autobiography and prediction for students.
